comment_text.ja79:1.1: A village headman conspires with bandits to leave a village helpless and ripe for the plunder.
comment_text.ja79:1.3: Āgamā is aorist singular. | See the nearly identical phrase at MN 76:53.5; here we have puttahatāya rather than puttamatāya, but both mean the same thing.
comment_text.ja79:1.4: The expression kharassara is used for the beating of a drum to announce an execution (SN 12.70:28.5).

translation_text.ja79:0.4: The Harsh Sound: a past life story
translation_text.ja79:1.1: When cows were plundered and killed,
translation_text.ja79:1.2: houses burned down, and people abducted,
translation_text.ja79:1.3: then came the son of she whose son is dead,
translation_text.ja79:1.4: sounding the harsh drum of war.

variant_text.ja79:1.4: ḍiṇḍimaṁ → deṇḍimaṁ (bj, sya1ed, sya2ed, pts-vp-pli1); ḍindimaṁ (mr)
